$comment: Power Pete, as powerpete.com and the Dynamics 365 Contact Center licensing calculator
use it. Same product, same design system, different paint.
The ramp is generated from the Power Pete palette rather than picked by eye: the
primary family is their purple, tinted toward white above 600 and toward their own
deep purple below it. Every pairing the product actually renders was checked against
WCAG AA and the weakest is 9.86 to 1, because a palette that looks right in a swatch
and fails at three to one is a product somebody cannot read.
What is NOT in here: anything true regardless of the colours. The product still runs
in Capgemini's subscription and still signs people in with their Capgemini account,
and those sentences stay as they are. A brand file that could change them would be a
brand file that could make the privacy page lie.
name: Power Pete
tagline: Tips & best practices for Dynamics 365 and the Power Platform
$rampComment: The family names are roles, not hues. Power Pete's primary is purple, so it fills the
blue slots; the secondary is their sky, which happens to be the same value Capgemini
uses; the tertiary is their mint.
$pdfComment: Taken from the calculator's own pdf block so a client who receives both recognises
them as one family: band is the deep purple, accent the lilac, and the series runs
lilac, blue, mint, amber. Coral is the marker, never a series.

copy.preparedBy: Prepared with the Power Platform Solution Analyzer from powerpete.com. Estimates are ranges from a rule catalogue, not a quotation.
